problem_markdown: Prove that the real solution set of $\sum_{k=1}^{70}k/(x-k)\ge5/4$ is a union of disjoint intervals whose total length is 1988.
solutions_markdown:
Let $F(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{70}k/(x-k)$. On each interval between consecutive poles it is strictly decreasing, with limits $+\infty$ and $-\infty$. On $(70,\infty)$ it decreases from $+\infty$ to zero, and for $x<1$ it is negative. Thus $F(x)=5/4$ has one root $r_k\in(k,k+1)$ for $k<70$ and one $r_{70}>70$. The solution intervals are $(k,r_k]$.

Put $P(x)=\prod_{j=1}^{70}(x-j)$ and $S=1+\cdots+70=2485$. Their endpoints are all 70 roots of
$$Q(x)=\tfrac54P(x)-\sum_{k=1}^{70}k\frac{P(x)}{x-k}.$$
The leading coefficients of $Q$ are $5/4$ and $-(5/4)S-S=-(9/4)S$. Vieta gives $\sum r_k=9S/5$. Therefore the total interval length is $\sum(r_k-k)=4S/5=1988$.
